title: The Loom and the Lantern
story:
James sat quietly upon a low wooden stool beside the steady, hypnotic rhythm of the loom. He watched as this man rhythmically worked the shuttle back and forth, weaving vibrant threads into long patterns of green and gold that reminded him faintly of the high canopies back home. Every pull of the wooden lever brought a familiar comfort, echoing the gentle sway of the jungle branches he had left behind so many days ago.

As the evening shadows lengthened across the flagstone floor, this man paused his work and reached into a small stoneware crock by the hearth. He pulled out a warm, roasted chestnut, offering it gently across the wooden bench to his small visitor. James accepted the morsel with a cautious nod, nibbling the soft treat as the fire cast a warm, flickering glow against the workshop's cluttered, yarn-draped walls.

Resting his tired feet, James unspooled the weathered leather strap around his shoulder and carefully checked his belongings. He touched the smooth green sea-glass, traced the edge of his brass map canister, and felt the comforting weight of his small magnifying lens. Here, surrounded by the scent of wool and wood smoke, the vast and intimidating city of Oakhaven felt small, safe, and entirely full of quiet wonders.
